root_cause.class: captured fused intermediate outputs had graph-pool-owned lifetime
root_cause.mechanism: The fused norm entry allocated norm_out and residual_out with torch.empty_like inside full-model HIP graph capture. Those custom-kernel intermediate pointers were owned and reused by the graph private pool across 72 fused sites. Their address/lifetime layout was unstable across fresh captures and later eager transitions, producing intermittent memory faults. Binding every captured site to persistent graph-stable caller-owned output storage removes graph-pool ownership from the custom fused outputs.
root_cause.scope: Fusion-specific failure after the base graph-padding sentinel fix

passing_controls: 15/15 graph servers where the fused backend declined during capture
isolation.interpretation: The common failing factor was a custom fused output allocated inside the captured full-model graph, not a collective algorithm, barrier, memory substrate, or numerical kernel defect.

fix.lifetime: one slot per GPT-OSS fused call site; 72-site forward parity returns to the same epoch only after all prior outputs have been consumed
fix.fallback: M above the one-shot threshold retains caller-owned dynamic outputs outside decode graph capture

non_fix_control.interpretation: Graph-pool layout is incidence-sensitive, as were KV-capacity and logging controls. Merely reserving memory is not the production contract; persistent per-site output ownership is retained because it removes the unsafe ownership class directly and passed the full formal campaign.

decision.reason: The stable implementation regresses decode median TPOT and output throughput with confidence intervals excluding zero.
decision.next_step: Do not deploy TP4 fusion; revisit only with a safe integration that recovers the explicit-copy/output-ownership overhead and clears a new paired campaign.
